column8: Wed 18 Nov: store only, background to rows 2 and 9 (who stood behind PACT); at most a 3f outside example; the bill was tuition for many families, not ten fixed dollar payments.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a store, who stood behind the promise was argued in court for years; quotes exact; IPS l.11 checked (the money goes straight into Treasuries), so the ten have no outside backer to argue about.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f outside example; Alabama's 72% target beside the first plan's 75% in 2027-2030 checked against NUMBERS 8s; 63.8% is Keel arithmetic; Alabama paid each term, the first plan bought all ten on 1 Jan 2033.
Wed 18 Nov: 3f background only; an allegation never a finding, dismissed on procedure (no demand on the board); the team's reason stays IPS l.9 (CANON A3).
Wed 18 Nov: 3f with row 45, a share-led promise already short at the top of the market (97.6% in 2007); for 3a say most of each payment owned in Jan 2027 and all ten from Jan 2028 (NUMBERS 1).

Wed 18 Nov: drop losses come in runs, which the 27 Sep model does not show (it draws independent years); say a miss needs several poor years, not a crash (NUMBERS 8s: 35.6% of misses had no year down 20%); the 76.5% is checked.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; news figures, and the $899m to $431m includes payouts and about 700 withdrawals, so never call it a market loss of half.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 19 (the bill rose in the same recession that sank the assets); Alabama's 33.1% is correct Keel arithmetic (1.130 x 1.072 x 1.099) and can sit in row 19's evidence.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a store, taxpayers' money kept PACT alive; IPS l.11 checked (anybody else's money); head row of the taxpayer cluster with rows 30 and 33.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a conceit turn, an appropriation not yet paid is pencil; a dissent, so name it as one; the conceit never enters Laura's words to co-sponsors.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f or 3e, the cut verified at source with the exact clause; supersedes store H5-070's news-only version of the settlement.

Wed 18 Nov: drop the 2.78 times, the PACT page does not say how the increases combine (and 24% then 23% may be levels, not steps); keep only that any restoring is a board's yearly choice, not a contract.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e aha, the funded ratio moved on what was promised, not on the money; the swings are 2011-2013 rulings (2018's 120.5% is not one); pairs with a dollar figure owned in Treasuries.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 31 (failed plans ended in bonds); Alabama's were short bonds, not matched by date, so the weaker example.
Wed 18 Nov: confirms claim 2 (was sued); no suit found fault on the merits; store only, never in 3f as a verdict.
Wed 18 Nov: 3f or 3e, two falls of about 25 points, each in a recession of the kind IPS l.9 names (checked); TIPS named only as GET's holding, never Laura's (Wharton ban).

Wed 18 Nov: 3a and 3e aha, the actuary priced the bill rising as the assets fell (-0.45); TNA l.7 checked (fixed in nominal dollars); for the facility a 3e limit only, never tends to for Taiwan costs (Q85).
Wed 18 Nov: 3f disanalogy, pooled plans refilled from new buyers; Laura has no money in after Jan 2028, so a 1 Jan 2033 miss could not be made up (NUMBERS 8s checked); absorbs row 29.
Wed 18 Nov: drop even a 1-in-67 set against the first plan's 1 in 31, two rates side by side read as a yardstick for high (CANON A4: IPS l.11 is its only definition); keep only who would pay.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a, a guarantee moves a loss and does not remove it; the statute was read only as the study cites it, so cite the study.
Wed 18 Nov: store, evidence under row 20 that new buyers paid for old losses; +39% is correct Keel arithmetic; read in part.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a, say Laura's $50,000 is fixed in dollars (TNA l.7) and no one can reprice it, not a Treasury's $50,000 is set in stone: five of the ten are iBond funds paying net asset value (CANON C2).
Wed 18 Nov: without the money doing anything is unsupported, GET's assets also rose with markets 2015-2025; say the tuition cut and premiums helped turn the deficit into a surplus.
Wed 18 Nov: store, College Illinois's mix after the crash, about 76% growth assets (Keel arithmetic 33.7 + 42.6 checked); the pre-2008 mix is a gap.
Wed 18 Nov: store for claim 3's deficits; 70.5% is correct Keel arithmetic ($1,282.0m against $1,818.3m).

Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 10 (taxpayers paid); $280m is correct Keel arithmetic; the FY22 report itself was not read.
